title: Why College & Career Readiness Can’t Wait Until Senior Year [New Research]
summary: New research from Panorama Education on college and career readiness highlights opportunities for earlier exploration, guidance, and pathway planning.
body_markdown:
## What we found


Career conversations with adults are limited.


Just 24% of high school students report spending a meaningful amount of time talking with adults at school about careers that could be a good fit, and 25% report spending a meaningful amount of time in conversations with professionals working in careers they're interested in.


College and career readiness and clarity about pathways do grow over time in high school.


For example, in 9th grade, 47% of students report a firm understanding of which courses they need to reach their college and career goals. By 12th grade, that rises to 62%.


However, some important college and career readiness gains may come too late.


Students report some of the biggest increases in career conversations and college exploration between grades 11 and 12.
